criteria.need: Solving the problem and user need (20%)

findings.title: A sign-off nobody can give holds the kitchen's weekly budget for seven days; the next judge's milk order has no options
steps: On a fresh server open /k/laakso and ask for Valio's example: 1,000 L lactose-free milk for next weekday.
Choose the first card and place the order: it waits for sign-off (EUR 1,322, over the EUR 1,000 limit).
Ask for the same thing again (a second judge).
findings.expected: The second request gets option cards; an order that can no longer be signed (quote expired) stops counting against the budget.
findings.actual: no_options. Every 10 L and 1 L product is excluded as over_budget (EUR 678 left of EUR 2,000), because the first, still-pending order counts as spent. Pending orders never expire and there is no way to cancel one.
findings.cause: web/src/core/orders.ts:266-273 spentThisWeek counts every pending_approval order created in the last 7 days, with no check of the quote's expiry; nothing moves a pending approval out of pending when its quote expires.
findings.fix: Count a pending order only until its quote expires (or expire the approval with the quote and log it), and add a cancel/withdraw call for the buyer and the agent.

findings.title: On a production build the demo kitchens' sign-offs cannot be given at all
steps: pnpm build && pnpm start (NODE_ENV=production) without DOCK_DEMO_TAP_APPROVAL.
On /k/laakso or /k/kaari place an order over the agent's limit.
GET /ui-api/kitchens/laakso/approval/<approvalId>.
findings.expected: The console shows a QR code or link with which the named (fictional) approver can sign, as in dev.
findings.actual: mode: view_only. The one-time link exists only in the in-memory outbox, which is 404 in production (/api/v1/dev/outbox). The order stays pending forever, and (F-PENDING-HOLDS-BUDGET) blocks the kitchen's budget.
findings.fix: Set DOCK_DEMO_TAP_APPROVAL=1 on the demo deployment, or give the demo kitchens a real approver path (join their approver role with a passkey from the wall), and say on screen who can sign.
findings.note: Whether the public deployment sets DOCK_DEMO_TAP_APPROVAL was not checked (out of scope); the visitor-kitchen path (scan the QR code) is not affected.

findings.title: Every visitor of /k/kaari or /k/laakso is the same agent: the 31st request in an hour gets 429 for everyone
steps: On a fresh server make 31 requests on /k/kaari within an hour (any amounts).
findings.expected: Each visitor's request is answered; the partner API is protected per visitor or per session, not per demo kitchen.
findings.actual: Request 31 returns 429 live_lookup_budget_exceeded: 'This agent already made 30 live price/availability lookups in the last 60 minutes'. Each intake costs 1-2 live lookups and each quote one more, so on a busy stand the shared demo kitchen goes dark after roughly 10-15 visitors and stays dark for the rest of the hour.
findings.cause: web/src/core/live-allowance.ts:17-21 (30 calls, 60 min, per org:agent) with web/src/server/console-kitchens.ts giving every console visitor the kitchen's one agent id.
findings.fix: Key the allowance by console session for the demo kitchens (or raise it there and cache live answers for a few minutes per product and date), and show the visitor a plain 'busy, try in N minutes' message.

findings.title: Anyone can read every kitchen's ledger, including request texts and kitchen memory, with no credentials
steps: Kaari opens a request with a private text.
With no Authorization header, GET /api/v1/ledger; or POST /ui-api/kitchens/kaari/call {method:GET,path:/api/v1/ledger} to read Laakso's.
findings.expected: A buyer sees its own organisation's entries; the wholesaler view needs wholesaler credentials; strangers see the chain head and verification only.
findings.actual: 200 with every entry of every organisation (request texts, quotes, prices, decisions, approver names), 480+ entries across 58 actors on one run.
findings.cause: web/src/app/api/v1/ledger/route.ts has no authenticate(); the console allow-list (web/src/app/ui-api/kitchens/[kitchen]/call/route.ts:22) forwards it and the route ignores the mandate.
findings.fix: Authenticate the ledger route and filter entries to the mandate's orgId (keep verify() over the whole chain and return only the head to others).

findings.title: The agent can 'confirm' a likely mistake itself, and the ledger records it as the head chef's confirmation
steps: As Kaari's agent (mandate only), POST /api/v1/intake 1,000 L milk: needs_confirmation, quantity_tenfold.
POST /api/v1/intake/<id>/concerns {by:'Sanna Koskinen (head chef)', responses:[{key, choice:'confirm'}]} with the same mandate.
findings.expected: A human-input step (confirming a likely tenfold slip) is answered only by the human, with a proof like the sign-off's; or the ledger at least says the agent relayed it unverified.
findings.actual: 200, state options_ready. Ledger: actor 'buyer:Sanna Koskinen (head chef)', 'Sanna Koskinen (head chef) confirmed as intended: 1,000 L ...'. The 'by' name is free text from the agent.
findings.cause: web/src/core/intake.ts:96-104 (by is z.string), respondToConcerns/answer/choose authorise with the agent's mandate only; the actor is built from 'by' (intake.ts:438).
findings.fix: Record these as 'relayed by agent X for <name>, unverified' and, for a confirmed tenfold or unusual quantity, carry it to sign-off (escalate) unless the confirmation carries a human proof.

findings.title: Substitution rules only apply when the agent declares a substitute; 'no substitutes' and the price cap can be walked around
steps: Mandate substitution.rule = none. Open a request for 20 x VA-1010.
Quote AR-2010 x 20 with substituteFor VA-1010: refused (holds). Quote AR-2010 x 20 without substituteFor and order it: committed.
Mandate within_preferences, +10 %. JP-3010 for VA-1010 is +25.6 %/L and fails; declaring it a substitute for VA-1201 instead passes substitute_price.
findings.expected: The gate knows what the request asked for (a product, or the intake's chosen card) and treats anything else as a substitute, judged against the requested product's price.
findings.actual: The undeclared substitute commits alone; the price check compares against whatever 'original' the agent names.
findings.cause: web/src/core/policy.ts:169-211 looks only at lines with substituteFor; web/src/core/quote.ts:157-170 takes req.substituteFor from the agent; the request (orders.ts PurchaseRequest) carries only free text, no product reference.
findings.fix: Store the requested product(s) (or the intake's card) on the request, have the quote mark every line not in it as a substitute for it, and compare prices against the requested product.

findings.title: Pending sign-offs, the sign-off screen and the live event stream of every kitchen are open to anyone
steps: Any kitchen's order goes to sign-off.
With no credentials: GET /api/v1/approvals, GET /api/v1/approvals/<id>, GET /api/v1/events?since=0.
findings.expected: Only the approver's phone (session cookie) and the kitchen's own console see a pending sign-off; the wall gets anonymised events.
findings.actual: All pending approvals of all organisations (org, agent, lines, total, reasons); the full sign-off view (kitchen, approver name, items, why); and an event stream replaying every organisation's events.
findings.cause: web/src/app/api/v1/approvals/route.ts ('APPROVER-AUTH SEAM: open today'), approvals/[approvalId]/route.ts GET, events/route.ts with no scope.
findings.fix: Require the approver session for /approvals and /approvals/{id}; give the wall its own event feed without org ids and amounts per kitchen, or with per-sandbox opt-in.

findings.title: A stranger can list visitors' kitchens and make their agents order, sending sign-off requests to other people's phones
steps: A visitor joins by QR code.
Anyone: GET /api/v1/sandboxes (lists every sbx_ id), POST /api/v1/sandboxes/<id>/demo-order.
findings.expected: Only the wall (or the visitor themselves) starts a visitor kitchen's demo order.
findings.actual: 201 with a new approval on the visitor's kitchen; repeated calls each create another sign-off request on that phone (and spend partner API lookups).
findings.cause: web/src/app/api/v1/sandboxes/[sandboxId]/demo-order/route.ts has no check; web/src/app/api/v1/sandboxes/route.ts lists all ids.
findings.fix: Require the visitor's session (or a wall token) for demo-order and drop sandbox ids from the public list (the wall can show names only).

findings.title: Anyone who knows a kitchen's slug acts as its agent through the console back end, including visitors' kitchens
steps: Take any sbx_ id from GET /api/v1/sandboxes.
POST /ui-api/kitchens/<sbx_id>/call with intake, choice and order calls.
findings.expected: A visitor's kitchen console is usable from the visitor's phone/session (or read-only for others).
findings.actual: The stranger opens an intake, confirms, chooses and commits an order within the visitor's EUR 500 limit, spending the visitor's weekly budget.
findings.cause: web/src/app/ui-api/kitchens/[kitchen]/call/route.ts attaches the kitchen's mandate to any caller (documented DEMO NOTE in console-kitchens.ts).
findings.fix: For sbx_ kitchens require the visitor's approver session cookie; keep the two demo kitchens open but rate-limited.

findings.title: The paid model interpreter is reachable anonymously through the console, with no rate limit or quota
findings.reproduce: curl -s -XPOST http://localhost:4311/ui-api/kitchens/kaari/call -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"method":"POST","path":"/api/v1/agent/interpret","body":{"text":"10 L milk for Tuesday"}}'
steps: Repeat the call above in a loop.
findings.expected: A per-session and global cap on model calls (and a cache for identical text), with 429 beyond it.
findings.actual: Every call is a paid model call (about 1.2 s each); no limit, no quota header.
findings.fix: Add a small token bucket per client and a global daily cap on interpret, and cache by (text, day).

findings.title: 'No options' leads with stock and delivery reasons when the budget is what blocked it
steps: As F-PENDING-HOLDS-BUDGET step 3.
findings.expected: 'Your weekly budget has EUR 678 left; this needs about EUR 1,322' first, with what to do.
findings.actual: 'Nothing on the short list can be delivered in time within the mandate: earliest delivery Thu 19 Nov is after Wed 18 Nov...; only 400 L in stock...' The four over_budget exclusions are cut off.
findings.cause: web/src/core/intake.ts:539-544 noOptionReason takes the first three distinct reasons in list order.
findings.fix: Order exclusion reasons by how many products they removed and lead with budget and cut-off, which the buyer can act on.

findings.title: A quote issued for one request can be placed as an order on another request
steps: Open requests A and B.
Quote 3 x VA-1001 on A.
POST /api/v1/orders {requestId: B, quoteToken: <A's quote>}.
findings.expected: Refused by quote_binding: the quote names request A.
findings.actual: Committed under B. The ledger shows the quote under A and the order under B; B's need-by date, intake state and kitchen memory are the ones applied.
findings.cause: web/src/core/policy.ts:106-111 quote_binding checks organisation, agent and mandate but not quote.requestId; web/src/core/orders.ts:583-597 never compares it with input.requestId.
findings.fix: Add requestId to quote_binding (one line in policy.ts) and a test.

findings.title: Between 00:00 and 02:00 Helsinki (03:00 in summer) the gate's latest delivery day is one day short
steps: In process: evaluatePolicy at 2026-11-13T22:00Z (Sat 00:00 Helsinki) with maxLeadDays 5 and a line delivered Thu 19 Nov.
findings.expected: Pass: Thursday is five Helsinki days ahead, as the intake counts it.
findings.actual: delivery_deadline fails: 'after the latest acceptable date 2026-11-18'. 14 of 144 sampled hours (every night, both DST sides).
findings.cause: web/src/core/policy.ts:160 and web/src/core/options.ts:213 use isoDate(addDays(now, n)), a UTC date; the intake uses localNow() in Europe/Helsinki.
findings.note: Rare on stage (night only), but an order the cards offer can then be refused by the gate.
